Faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before you start

q1.q: Who are the mentors on Connectus?
q1.a: Mentors are applicants and graduates of top universities worldwide who went through the admissions process themselves and now help others do the same. Many are Bolashak, Chevening, DAAD, and other scholarship recipients. Every mentor is vetted and authenticated — only carefully selected, competency-checked candidates work on the platform.

q2.a: The first consultation is a get-to-know-you call where you discuss your goals and plan. Mentors set their own prices for services, and you see the full cost upfront. No hidden fees.

q3.a:
The applicant sends the mentor a consultation request. The mentor can accept or decline — for example, if they already have a lot of active applicants. Once accepted, a chat opens right on the platform, and all communication stays inside Connectus.

An important note on safety: all discussions should stay on the platform. If you exchange personal contacts (phone, messengers, email) and work outside Connectus, we can't take responsibility for the quality of the work and won't be able to help if a dispute comes up.

q4.q: What if the mentor isn't the right fit?
q4.a: The first consultation is a get-to-know-you call. If you feel the mentor isn't the right fit, you're free to choose someone else.

q5.q: Why is Connectus useful for parents?
q5.a:
Applying abroad involves hundreds of details: choosing a country and university, exams, essays, deadlines, grants, visas. Figuring it all out alone is nearly impossible, and a single mistake can cost a year — or your child's dream.

Connectus gives you direct access to people who've already walked that path — graduates of MIT, Oxbridge, TU Munich, Bolashak and Chevening scholars. They'll tell you how it really works, help build a plan tailored to your child, and save you months of searching for information online.

q1.a: An applicant or graduate of any university abroad. What matters most is real admissions experience and a willingness to help others. Scholarship recipients are especially welcome.

q2.q: How much time does mentoring take?
q2.a: As much as you want. You can hold 1-2 consultations a week. You're fully in control of your own schedule.

q3.a: The applicant pays for the service through the platform. Once it's completed, we transfer the money to you, minus the platform fee.

q4.a: 15% per transaction. You set your own price and see exactly how much you'll receive before publishing a service.

q5.q: Do I need a degree or certificate?
q5.a: No. Real experience of applying abroad is enough. We review your profile and confirm your university.
